correctness.rationale: For every missing-edge pair (a,b), its common neighborhood contains S-a-b ones among N-2 vertices; a universal vertex x sees S-x ones among N-1. The exact tie rules give consensus off critical levels and an involution on central balanced states when u is even. For even u, the middle layer has binom(2r+u,r+u/2) periodic states and either 2^r extra fixed states only when u=0 or no balanced fixed states when u>=2; fixed and 2-orbit formulas follow. For odd u, only S=h or h+1 can avoid immediate consensus; every pair becomes 00/11 and universal bits agree after one update. Counting the possible alternating pair profiles yields u=1, odd h with h=r+(u-1)/2, and the parity/size extinction conditions for u>=3; after at most three updates any nonperiodic configuration enters a uniform consensus. An independent literal-neighborhood binary state enumeration r=1..4,u=0..4 (up to 12 vertices) matched fixed counts and primitive 2-cycle formulas; the exact weighted pair-profile verifier source independently establishes finite instances.
residual_risks: The general all-r,u assertion uses case analysis, not the finite census. In u=0 the graph is a regular complete multipartite graph with parts of size two; for u>=1 mixed singleton parts change tie behaviour.
